findings.summary: The ci.yml half and fixtures A, B and D copy policy.rs almost line for line; only the BUILD_PATHS check (fixture E) is new.
findings.evidence: xtask/tests/policy.rs:842-934 already has compiled_in_files, hash_files_globs, covers and check_athena_bin_keys. Its test at 973-998 already runs the same fixtures: remove 'docs/system-facts.md' with replacen, narrow to 'crates/**/*.rs', and add docs/new-compiled-in.md and crates/x/prompts/new.md. The plan's A, B and D repeat these. Fix: Keep the copy, since criterion 2 requires it, but keep it small. The CHANGELOG and D154 should say plainly that the ci.yml half repeats policy.rs and that the new protection is the BUILD_PATHS check. That way a later job can merge the two scanners, for example by having policy.rs also assert BUILD_PATHS once xtask is in scope.
findings.location: Decision 3 / Demonstration criterion 3 (fixtures A, B, D)

findings.summary: The Unreleased-only changelog test breaks at the next release, so the claim that it is cheap to maintain at release time is wrong.
findings.evidence: The plan splits on `## [Unreleased]` and stops at the next `## [`, as reading.rs:7829-7834 does. Once the entry moves under a version heading, the three job ids leave that window and the test fails. Fix: Either search the whole CHANGELOG.md for the three ids and `compiled-in` (it still fails without the entry), or keep the Unreleased window and change the rationale to say the test must be updated at release, as the reading.rs precedent must be.

findings.summary: The ontology class already has its own content check (D152). The entry should cite it rather than present this change as the 0wtc mechanism.
findings.evidence: docs/decisions.md:4111 has D152 · 'The ontology test compares each term with its governing sources, and excuses are bounded'. Fix: In the CHANGELOG entry and D154, say that 0wtc's instance of the cause is already enforced by D152's ontology test, and that this change applies the same rule (check the declared list against its source) to BUILD_PATHS and the CI key.
findings.location: CHANGELOG.md entry / D154: how job 0wtc is addressed

findings.summary: A comment-only edit to a governance file adds risk and buys little.
findings.evidence: The plan changes no key, step or glob; the link between the two checks is already recorded in the new test's doc comment and in D154. Fix: Consider dropping the ci.yml edit. If it is kept, run `cargo test -p xtask --test policy`, as step 7 already plans.

findings.summary: The drain.rs doc comment does list the paths, so it will go stale unless it is updated.
findings.evidence: drain.rs:109 lists `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `setup.sh` ([`touches_build`]); decisions.md:3645 and 3663 also describe BUILD_PATHS. Fix: Make the drain.rs:109 update unconditional, or reword it to point to BUILD_PATHS instead of listing paths.

summary: I read status.rs, all include_str!/include_bytes! uses under crates/, the athena-bin keys in ci.yml, xtask/tests/policy.rs lines 780–1007, the drain test, and the D-numbers in decisions.md. The plan's claims hold up against the code. BUILD_PATHS (status.rs:20) has only five entries, and the matching logic is inlined at status.rs:25, so it needs the new `list_touches` seam. athena.toml (athena-gate/src/lib.rs:33) and docs/system-facts.md (briefs.rs:1230) are compiled in before the first #[cfg(test)] line, yet BUILD_PATHS leaves them out. That is a real instance of the declared-list-never-checked cause, and the drain rebuild/stale-build logic gets it wrong today. Every include of defaults.toml in production files sits in a test module (for example defaults.rs:89 is inside the mod at :85), so leaving it out is justified. ci.yml has exactly nine athena-bin key lines. D154 is the next free number. The drain test at drain.rs:1421 lists no path that the extension would flip. Fixture E runs against the production matcher through `list_touches`, so it is not a double. Fixture B, built from the pre-fix kq9v key, meets criterion 3. On soundness, the approach is not a crude heuristic. The main cost is that the ci.yml half copies an existing checker almost line for line, which the plan admits and which criterion 2 forces. The new value is the BUILD_PATHS check. I found only minor findings and nits.
